title: Chicago Pile-1: the first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction
summary: On 2 December 1942, an experiment led by Enrico Fermi at the University of Chicago started the first human-made self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction in Chicago Pile-1, the first artificial nuclear reactor. Built under Stagg Field's stands for the Manhattan Project, it showed a chain reaction could be controlled and that military use of nuclear energy was feasible.

as_recorded.value: On 2 December 1942, the first human-made self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction

where.modern_name: Site of the former Stagg Field west stands, University of Chicago, Illinois (S. Ellis Ave. between E. 56th and 57th Sts.)

importance.justification: First controlled nuclear chain reaction; a foundational step of the Manhattan Project and the nuclear age.
